text: Chris Donisi named winner of Logan Airport's Voice of Logan contest. Voice of Logan is trending after Massport named Chris Donisi, a pipefitter, the new voice of Logan Airport's overhead announcements on Thursday. The announcement came as the contest's winner was revealed.. Massport, the state agency that runs Boston's Logan International Airport, chose Chris Donisi as the new voice for its public address announcements. Donisi works as a pipefitter. Sources differ on his hometown, with one saying Arlington, Massachusetts, and another saying Burlington, Massachusetts. He was announced as the winner on Thursday morning. The contest drew thousands of applicants. One account puts applicants above 5,200, while another says more than 6,000 people auditioned and 35,000 people voted. Donisi will replace Joe LoGiudice, who has given about 25 years of service to the airport's announcements. LoGiudice is not retiring from Massport and will keep his other airport duties.

What is Voice of Logan? Chris Donisi named winner, Thursday. Voice of Logan is a public contest run by Massport, the state agency that operates Boston Logan International Airport, to choose the voice for its overhead announcements. Chris Donisi, a pipefitter from Massachusetts, was named the winner on Thursday morning.. Massport announced Chris Donisi as the new Voice of Logan on Thursday morning, ending the nearly 25-year run of Joe LoGiudice on the airport's public address system.. Donisi will take over the airport's recorded announcements from Joe LoGiudice, whose voice has been used for nearly 25 years. The contest sought a speaker with an authentic Boston accent who could make local travelers feel at home. Donisi said his mother urged him to audition, and he called the win "unreal" in an interview on Good Morning America. Sources differ on his hometown: one names Arlington, Massachusetts, and another names Burlington, Massachusetts. In a statement, Donisi said he was born just outside Boston in East Arlington. Massport reported that more than 6,000 people auditioned and 35,000 people voted, while another count put applicants above 5,200. LoGiudice is not leaving Massport. He will keep his other airport duties, a job he has held since graduating from Bridgewater State University in 1993.
